rule: A source is placed on the left–right line by its recorded labels. Labels that are positions (far-left, left-wing, centre-left, centrist, centre-right, right-wing, far-right) are used as they are. Only when a source has none of those, other labels are placed if English Wikipedia's article on that ideology (or on liberalism in the source's country, for "liberal") states one position for it as a whole; a label defined there as a variant of an ideology already placed takes that ideology's position. Where the article describes the ideology on more than one side, or does not say, the label is not placed. A label with two positions counts half for each; a source with several placed labels is split equally. "Liberal" is placed only for a source with exactly one recorded country, and only for the countries listed.
